intro.text: 今天这批内容有两条并行的主线。一条关于「怎么做对」：Madhu Guru 和 Peter Yang 在同一天把 AI 评测讲透了——评测真正的功夫不在测最终答案，而在把你对每一步的判断编码进去。另一条关于「基础设施」：Rauchg 说智能正在变便宜、gateway 是必然，Thibault 说 2026 是企业开始认真对待模型效率的一年。而 Garry Tan 的一句话预测则点出了所有旧系统的命运：系统记录要么变成 AI 的驾驭装置，要么被 agent 取代。

sections.title: Making Evals a Craft / 把评测做成一门手艺
sections.desc: 评测正在从玄学变成可诊断的工程：不是测最终答案，而是把你对每一步的判断编码进去。

rewrite: Meta's Senior Director of AI Madhu Guru continues his series on building great evals with the 'Goldilocks principle': your evals should measure at the level of each intermediate job-to-be-done, not just the final answer.

His example: a financial analysis agent that outputs a stock recommendation. If you only check whether the agent picked the 'right' stock, you learn nothing when it's wrong. But if you score each stage separately — understanding the client (92%), gathering evidence (92%), analyzing data (70%), making the recommendation (75%) — you immediately know the data-analysis step is where to dig.
The rule: not too granular, not too coarse — just granular enough to diagnose and act. It's the most actionable eval-framing advice in the feed today.
original: How to build great evals - part 7. The Goldilocks principle for eval construction. Your evals should measure at the level of the various jobs to be done, not just the final answer.
If the final recommendation is wrong, a well designed eval set would tell you: Client understanding: 92%, Evidence extraction: 92%, Data analysis: 70%, Recommendation: 75%
Not too granular. Not too coarse. Just right. Make your eval set as granular as you need to diagnose and act.

rewrite: Meta 的 AI 高级总监 Madhu Guru 继续他的「如何做好评测」系列，这次讲的是「金发姑娘原则」：评测应该测量每个中间环节的 job-to-be-done，而不是只看最终答案。
他举的例子是一个做股票推荐的金融分析 agent。如果你只检查它有没有选中「正确」的股票，那它错的时候你什么都学不到。但如果分开给每个阶段打分——理解客户 92%、收集证据 92%、数据分析 70%、给出推荐 75%——你立刻就知道该去深挖数据分析这一步。
规则是：不要太细，也不要太粗，细到刚好能诊断并采取行动就行。这是今天 feed 里关于评测最可落地的一条。
original: 如何做好评测第 7 篇：评测构建的「金发姑娘原则」。评测应该在各个 job-to-be-done 的层级去测，而不只是最终答案。
如果最终推荐错了，设计良好的评测集会告诉你：客户理解 92%、证据提取 92%、数据分析 70%、推荐 75%。
不要太细，不要太粗，刚刚好。让评测集细到足以诊断和行动。

rewrite: Peter Yang relays a clean mental model for AI evals from Shreya Shankar (co-author, with Hamel Husain, of the industry-standard AI evals course): there are two types — top-down and bottom-up.

Top-down evals ask: given only a task description in a vacuum, what would you come up with? Claude is great at helping you brainstorm these. Bottom-up evals are the harder half: looking at many real sample outputs and externalizing your gut feedback into a checkable rule. Shreya's blunt verdict — 'Claude is very, very bad at coming up with bottom-up evals. That's all you.'
It pairs neatly with Madhu Guru's point the same day: the real work of evals isn't testing the final answer, it's encoding your judgment about each step.
original: There are two types of AI evals - tops down and bottoms up. From @sh_reya:
Think of top-down as: If you're in a vacuum, just given the task description, what would you come up with? Claude does a very good job of helping you with these top-down evals.

Bottom-up evals are the other half. When you look at lots and lots of sample outputs, what is your gut feedback that you want externalized into evals? Claude is very, very bad at coming up with bottom-up evals. That's all you.

rewrite: Peter Yang 转述了 Shreya Shankar（和 Hamel Husain 合著业内标杆 AI evals 课程）给的一个清晰模型：AI 评测有两种——自上而下和自下而上。
自上而下评测问的是：如果把你放在真空里，只给任务描述，你会想出什么？Claude 很擅长帮你头脑风暴这类评测。自下而上评测是更难的另一半：看大量真实样本输出，把你内心的直觉反馈外化成可检查的规则。Shreya 的判断很直接——「Claude 在做自下而上评测这件事上非常非常差，这全靠你自己。」
这和同一天 Madhu Guru 的观点正好呼应：评测真正的功夫不在测最终答案，而在于把你对每一步的判断编码进去。
original: AI 评测有两种：自上而下和自下而上。引自 @sh_reya。
自上而下：在真空里只给任务描述，你会想出什么？Claude 很擅长帮你做这类评测。
自下而上是另一半：看大量样本输出，把你内心的直觉反馈外化成评测。Claude 非常非常不擅长做自下而上的评测，这全靠你。

sections.title: Cheaper Intelligence, Critical Infrastructure / 更便宜的智能，关键的基础设施
sections.desc: 推理成本下降让用量暴涨，模型效率与可靠性变成企业的核心关切，gateway 成了必答题。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch points to a concrete data point for a trend everyone senses but few quantify: OpenAI Sol's price reductions and discounts on Vercel AI Gateway have made Sol Vercel's fastest-growing frontier model.

His two takeaways: first, demand for intelligence is highly elastic — as inference costs fall, usage grows fast. Second, if you're not routing through a gateway, you're missing the price volatility that lowers operating costs and increases margins.
His conclusion: the router/gateway space heating up was inevitable. As model prices swing, the people who win are the ones with infrastructure to shop around.
original: Intelligence is getting cheaper. @OpenAI Sol's price reductions & discounts on Vercel AI Gateway have made Sol our fastest-growing frontier model.
This shows ① that the demand for intelligence is highly elastic: as inference costs fall, usage grows rapidly.

② If you're not using a gateway, you're missing out on this incredible price volatility, which lowers your operating costs and increases your margins. It's no wonder the router space has heated up… gateways are inevitable.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 给一个大家都感受到却很少有人量化的趋势提供了具体数据：OpenAI Sol 的降价加上 Vercel AI Gateway 上的折扣，让 Sol 成了 Vercel 上增长最快的前沿模型。
他的两个结论：第一，对智能的需求弹性很高——推理成本一降，用量就快速涨。第二，如果你不通过 gateway 来路由，就会错过这种剧烈的价格波动，而它恰恰能降低运营成本、提高毛利。
他的收尾：路由/gateway 赛道升温是必然的。当模型价格大幅波动时，赢家是那些有基础设施可以货比三家的人。
original: 智能正在变便宜。OpenAI Sol 的降价和 Vercel AI Gateway 上的折扣，让 Sol 成为我们增长最快的前沿模型。
① 智能需求弹性很高：推理成本下降，用量快速增长。
② 不用 gateway 就会错过价格波动，它降低运营成本、提高毛利。router 赛道升温不奇怪，gateway 是必然。

rewrite: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux (who works on Codex) makes a prediction that reads like a mission statement: 2026 is the year companies start seriously caring about model efficiency and reliability, because AI has become critical infrastructure.

The same weekend, he announced a Codex usage reset had been propagated to accounts along with fixes for the usage issues flagged the day before — a small, concrete example of reliability work happening in real time, with more promised for tomorrow.
The thread: reliability is no longer a nice-to-have when the model is part of your production stack.
original: 2026 is the year companies start seriously caring about model efficiency and reliability as it becomes critical infrastructure

Good Sunday. Reset has been propagated to accounts and we landed some fixes to usage for things mentioned yesterday as issues we found. You should feel a positive difference. More to come tomorrow and will keep communicating.

rewrite: OpenAI 负责 Codex 的 Thibault Sottiaux 给出了一个读起来像使命宣言的预测：2026 年是企业开始真正重视模型效率和可靠性的一年，因为 AI 正在变成关键基础设施。
同个周末，他宣布 Codex 的用量重置已经推送到账户，并落地了针对前一天发现的用量问题的一些修复——这是可靠性工作在实时进行的一个小而具体的例子，还预告了明天会有更多。
主线很清晰：当模型成了你生产栈的一部分，可靠性就不再是加分项了。
original: 2026 是企业开始真正重视模型效率和可靠性的一年，因为它正在成为关键基础设施。
周日好。重置已推送到账户，我们落地了针对昨天提到的用量问题的一些修复。你应该能感受到正向的变化。明天还有更多，会持续沟通。

sections.title: The Open, Visual Agent Stack / 开放且可视的 Agent 技术栈
sections.desc: agent 栈的走向是开放协议加可视化界面——Unix 式的组合，而不是围墙花园。

rewrite: In a second post, Guillermo Rauch lays out Vercel's philosophy for extending fx (the agent framework): open protocols over proprietary lock-in.

The stack: MCP for model-context connections, Skills (agentskills.io) and Plugins (agent-plugins.org) for capability packaging, and — his favorite — Unix itself: small programs that do one thing well and compose by calling each other.

The goal is embeddability: a libfx you can build your own CLI, background agent, or software factory on, local or in the cloud. It's a bet that the agent stack will look like the web did — standards and composition, not walled gardens.
original: Our philosophy on extending fx: open protocols. MCP (modelcontextprotocol.io), Skills (agentskills.io), Plugins (agent-plugins.org).

And the best one, Unix: ① Small programs that do one thing well and compose by calling other programs. ② libfx that enables embeddability into more complex programs. You should be able to build your own CLI, background agent, software factory. Local or cloud.

rewrite: 第二条帖子里，Guillermo Rauch 阐述了 Vercel 扩展 fx（agent 框架）的哲学：用开放协议，而不是专有锁定。
这套栈是：MCP 负责模型-上下文连接，Skills（agentskills.io）和 Plugins（agent-plugins.org）负责能力的打包，以及他最喜欢的 Unix 本身——小程序做好一件事，通过调用其他程序来组合。
目标是可嵌入性：一个 libfx，让你能在上面构建自己的 CLI、后台 agent、软件工厂，本地或云端都行。这是一次对 agent 栈会像当年的 web 一样走向「标准和组合」而非「围墙花园」的下注。
original: 我们扩展 fx 的哲学：开放协议。MCP（modelcontextprotocol.io）、Skills（agentskills.io）、Plugins（agent-plugins.org）。
最好的是 Unix：① 小程序做好一件事，通过调用其他程序来组合。② libfx 实现可嵌入性。你应该能构建自己的 CLI、后台 agent、软件工厂。本地或云端。

rewrite: Peter Steinberger (OpenClaw + OpenAI) makes the case for moving agent interaction beyond the terminal: 'cli is nice, having UI visualizations and your team where you work is nicer.'

He's been dogfooding it literally — he added the rotation USB protocol to OpenClaw, told his claw to 'look around', and watched it have fun with a 360° webcam. The agent stopped being a text stream and became something that perceives and moves.
The signal: the agent interface is shifting from chat window to a visual, embodied workspace — and it's happening on consumer webcams, not just research rigs.
original: cli is nice, having UI visualizations and your team where you work is nicer. https://t.co/OFmkkkq6l5
I added the rotation USB protocol to https://t.co/kyF8ap5Pq6 and told my claw to look around- now it's having fun with my 360 webcam.

rewrite: Peter Steinberger（OpenClaw + OpenAI）为把 agent 交互带出终端给出了理由：「cli 很好，但在你工作的地方有 UI 可视化和你的团队更好。」
他自己在字面意义上做了实验——给 OpenClaw 加了旋转 USB 协议，让他的 claw「四处看看」，然后看着它跟一个 360° 摄像头玩得很开心。agent 不再只是文本流，而变成了能感知、能转动的东西。
信号是：agent 的界面正在从聊天窗口转向可视化、具身的工作空间——而且这事发生在消费级摄像头上，不只是研究设备上。
original: cli 很好，但在你工作的地方有 UI 可视化和你的团队更好。
我给 OpenClaw 加了旋转 USB 协议，让 claw 四处看看——现在它正跟我的 360° 摄像头玩得开心。

sections.title: The Stakes: Systems, Agents & Operators / 赌注：系统、Agent 与操作者
sections.desc: 旧系统面临被 agent 取代的压力，而会指挥 agent 的人类正在变成一种新职业。

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan drops a one-line prediction with big implications for enterprise software: 'systems of record will need to become AI harnesses or face replacement by agents.'

The thesis: the databases of truth that businesses run on (CRM, ERP, ticketing) were built for humans to read and update. If they don't become the substrate that agents act through — reading state, taking action, writing back — a new generation of agent-native tools will route around them.
It's the sharpest articulation yet of the 'adapt or be replaced' pressure now facing the incumbent SaaS giants.
original: Prediction: systems of record will need to become AI harnesses or face replacement by agents

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan 抛出了一条对企业软件影响深远的一句话预测：「系统记录（systems of record）要么变成 AI 驾驭装置（AI harnesses），要么被 agent 取代。」
这个论点的逻辑是：企业赖以运转的「事实数据库」（CRM、ERP、工单系统）本来是为人类读取和更新而建的。如果它们不能变成 agent 借以行动的基础——读取状态、执行动作、写回结果——那么新一代 agent 原生的工具就会绕过它们。
这是到目前为止对现有 SaaS 巨头所面临的「要么进化、要么被取代」压力最尖锐的表达。
original: 预测：系统记录要么变成 AI 驾驭装置，要么被 agent 取代。

rewrite: Peter Yang shares a concrete glimpse of the emerging 'AI-fluent operator' role: his human assistant Char has spent six months using Claude Code and Codex to run podcast post-production, draft show notes, and make clips — and has built up customized copies of Peter's AI skills for his own workflows.
The thesis: the best assistants today aren't the ones who type fastest, but the ones who know how to direct AI agents. Human judgment plus agent leverage is becoming its own job category.
(Note: the post is a paid promotion for the talent marketplace Oceans, but the workflow detail is what matters.)
original: I've been working with Char, my (human!) assistant from @oceanstalent for 6 months. I think the best assistants today need to know how to work with AI agents.
Char uses Claude Code and Codex to help me run podcast post-production, draft show notes, and make clips. He's made copies of my AI skills and tailored them for his own workflows over time.

rewrite: Peter Yang 让我们瞥见了正在出现的「懂 AI 的操作者」这一新角色：他的人类助理 Char 花了六个月，用 Claude Code 和 Codex 帮他做播客后期、起草 show notes、剪 clip——还逐渐把自己复制的 Peter 的 AI skills 调成了自己的专属工作流。
论点是：如今最好的助理不是打字最快的，而是最会指挥 AI agent 的。人类判断力叠加 agent 杠杆，正在变成一种独立的职业类型。
（注：这条是给人才市场 Oceans 的付费推广，但真正有价值的是里面那条工作流细节。）
original: 我和我的（人类！）助理 Char 合作了 6 个月。我认为如今最好的助理需要懂得如何与 AI agent 协作。
Char 用 Claude Code 和 Codex 帮我做播客后期、起草 show notes、剪 clip。他复制了我的 AI skills 并逐渐调成自己的工作流。
